questions.prompt: Which technique prevents data leakage when scaling features during cross-validation?
options: Fitting the scaler inside each cross-validation fold using a Pipeline
Scaling the entire dataset before splitting into train and test sets
Normalizing test labels along with features
Removing all outliers prior to splitting
questions.explanation: Fitting scalers only on training folds within a Pipeline ensures test fold statistics do not leak into model training.

questions.prompt: What metric is most appropriate for evaluating a binary classification model on a heavily imbalanced dataset (e.g. 99% negative, 1% positive)?
options: PR-AUC / Precision-Recall F1-score
Standard Accuracy
Mean Squared Error
Explained Variance
questions.explanation: On imbalanced datasets, a trivial model predicting the majority class achieves 99% accuracy; Precision, Recall, and PR-AUC properly reflect positive class detection.

questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) regularization?
options: L1 adds the absolute sum of weights and can drive coefficients exactly to zero for feature selection; L2 adds the squared sum and shrinks weights smoothly
L1 shrinks weights towards infinity while L2 shrinks them to zero
L2 can only be applied to decision tree algorithms
L1 and L2 are identical in effect
questions.explanation: L1 penalty induces sparsity by forcing non-informative feature weights to zero, acting as automatic feature selection.

questions.prompt: Why must you call `optimizer.zero_grad()` before `loss.backward()` in a typical PyTorch training loop?
options: PyTorch accumulates gradients on every backward pass by default instead of overwriting them
It resets model weights to random initialization
It frees GPU memory by deleting the computational graph
It normalizes the learning rate automatically
questions.explanation: PyTorch accumulates gradients across iterations unless explicitly cleared with zero_grad().

questions.prompt: What is the role of `model.eval()` and `torch.no_grad()` during model inference?
options: model.eval() configures layers like Dropout and BatchNorm for evaluation; torch.no_grad() disables gradient tracking to save compute and memory
Both functions convert floating point tensors to integers
They compile PyTorch code into C++ binaries
They upload the model weights to Hugging Face Hub
questions.explanation: model.eval() toggles inference behavior on layers (e.g. disables dropout, uses running batch statistics), while torch.no_grad() stops autograd history tracking.

questions.prompt: How does the Vanishing Gradient problem manifest in deep neural networks, and which mechanism mitigates it in ResNet architectures?
options: Gradients become exponentially small as they backpropagate through deep layers; residual skip connections allow gradients to flow directly without attenuation
Weights grow to infinity; softmax layers divide by the learning rate
The model predicts the same value for every input; resolved by adding more fully-connected layers
The GPU runs out of memory; resolved by increasing batch size
questions.explanation: Skip connections (f(x) + x) provide a direct gradient pathway during backpropagation, bypassing multiplicative weight decay.

questions.prompt: What is the primary role of a vector embedding in a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline?
options: To represent semantic meaning as dense floating-point coordinates for similarity retrieval
To encrypt sensitive documents in the database
To compress text files for faster network transmission
To parse JSON schemas into SQL tables
questions.explanation: Vector embeddings project textual content into semantic vector spaces where cosine distance measures thematic similarity.

questions.prompt: Why is document chunking with overlap critical when preparing context for vector search?
options: It preserves context across sentence boundaries and prevents information loss at chunk edges
It reduces the total number of vectors in the database
It converts text into relational tables
It removes all punctuation automatically
questions.explanation: Chunk overlap ensures concepts or phrases straddling chunk limits are captured in full context by the embedding model.

questions.prompt: How does Hybrid Search improve retrieval accuracy compared to pure dense vector search in RAG?
options: It combines dense vector semantic search with sparse keyword search (e.g. BM25) using reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) to capture both semantic meaning and exact keywords
It searches both MySQL and MongoDB simultaneously
It generates images and audio alongside text
It replaces language models with deterministic if-else rules
questions.explanation: Dense embeddings excel at conceptual meaning but often miss specific identifiers, part numbers, or rare terms that BM25 handles cleanly.

questions.prompt: What is 'Few-Shot Prompting'?
options: Providing the LLM with a small set of demonstration input-output examples directly in the context window before asking for the target completion
Training a model from scratch with only 5 epochs
Executing model inference only during off-peak hours
Restricting prompt length to under 10 tokens
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting conditions the model on exemplary pairs within the prompt context without modifying underlying weights.

questions.prompt: What does Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) do during parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)?
options: Freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into Transformer attention layers, drastically reducing trainable parameters
Quantizes the model to 1-bit weights
Deletes 50% of the attention heads randomly
Converts language models into convolutional neural networks
questions.explanation: LoRA freezes the base weights W0 and decomposes weight updates into product matrices B × A where rank r << d, lowering memory and VRAM requirements.

questions.prompt: What is catastrophic forgetting in the context of fine-tuning foundational models, and how can it be mitigated?
options: The model loses its generalized knowledge and reasoning when trained intensely on a narrow task; mitigated by mixing in general alignment data or using parameter-efficient tuning like LoRA
The GPU cache memory overflows during training; mitigated by rebooting
The token dictionary deletes special characters; mitigated by UTF-8 encoding
The model hallucinates citation URLs; mitigated by temperature = 0
questions.explanation: Catastrophic forgetting occurs when full weight adjustments overwrite pre-existing representations; LoRA and replay buffers preserve original model capacity.

questions.prompt: In Random Forest classifiers, what does 'Bagging' (Bootstrap Aggregation) accomplish?
options: Trains each tree on a random sample with replacement and subsets of features, reducing overall model variance without increasing bias
Aggregates predictions by computing the geometric mean of training errors
Prunes decision trees to a maximum depth of 2
Forces all decision trees to share identical split thresholds
questions.explanation: Bootstrapping creates diverse, decorrelated trees whose averaged predictions yield lower variance than individual deep trees.

questions.prompt: How does Gradient Boosting (e.g. XGBoost, LightGBM) differ fundamentally from Random Forest?
options: Gradient Boosting builds trees sequentially to predict the pseudo-residuals of preceding trees, whereas Random Forest trains independent trees in parallel
Gradient Boosting only works with text data
Random Forest minimizes gradient loss via backpropagation
Gradient Boosting cannot handle non-linear decision boundaries
questions.explanation: Boosting is an additive, sequential ensemble that optimizes a differentiable loss function by fitting each new learner to the negative gradient of the loss.

questions.prompt: What is the function of the Softmax activation layer in multi-class classification neural networks?
options: Transforms unnormalized logits into a valid probability distribution that sums to 1.0
Clamps negative values to zero like ReLU
Computes the Euclidean distance between feature vectors
Extracts spatial features from image tensors
questions.explanation: Softmax exponentiates logits and divides each by the sum of exponentials, yielding normalized probabilities.

questions.prompt: What does the PyTorch `DataLoader` abstraction provide during training?
options: Automated batching, shuffling, multi-process data loading, and pin_memory support for GPU transfers
Direct SQL querying of remote databases
Automatic code translation to ONNX
Automatic hyperparameter optimization via genetic algorithms
questions.explanation: DataLoader wraps a Dataset to provide mini-batch streaming, worker process parallelism, and optional memory pinning.

questions.prompt: What index algorithm is commonly used in vector databases for fast approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on millions of high-dimensional vectors?
options: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)
B-Tree index
Inverted bitmap index
Hash table
questions.explanation: HNSW builds multi-layer proximity graphs offering logarithmic search scaling for high-dimensional cosine and Euclidean distance queries.

questions.prompt: What is the function of 'Temperature' in LLM text generation sampling?
options: Controls the flatness of the softmax probability distribution: lower values produce more deterministic, conservative output; higher values increase diversity
Controls the clock speed and thermal throttling of the GPU
Measures the confidence score of the input tokenizer
Sets the maximum execution time of the inference request
questions.explanation: Dividing logits by temperature before softmax sharpens the distribution (low temp) or flattens it (high temp).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Principal Component Analysis (PCA)?
options: Dimensionality reduction by finding orthogonal axes that maximize data variance
Clustering data points into k distinct spherical clusters
Supervised regression for predicting continuous target values
Generating synthetic tabular data using GANs
questions.explanation: PCA projects data onto principal eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, capturing the greatest variance in descending orthogonal directions.

questions.prompt: In Transformer self-attention, why is the dot product of Query and Key scaled by `1 / sqrt(d_k)`?
options: To prevent large dot product magnitudes in high dimensions from pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely tiny gradients
To normalize vector magnitude to unit length
To convert floating point precision to integer values
To ensure attention weights sum to zero
questions.explanation: As d_k grows, dot products grow large in variance, pushing softmax into saturation where gradients vanish; 1/sqrt(d_k) stabilizes variance to 1.

projects.prompt:

Requirements:
1. Ingest text, split into overlapping chunks, and generate dense embeddings.
2. Store embeddings with metadata in a vector store.
3. Given a user query, perform top-k semantic search.
4. Assemble an augmented prompt injecting the retrieved context.
5. Implement a fallback when retrieved similarity is below threshold.

rubric.label: Semantic Search Accuracy
rubric.description: Cosine similarity or ANN distance calculation correctly ranks most relevant chunks.

rubric.label: Thresholding & Groundedness
rubric.description: Handles unanswerable queries gracefully with similarity threshold check to avoid hallucinations.

rubric.label: Modularity & Extensibility
rubric.description: Clean separation of embedder, retriever, vector index, and synthesis layers.
